summary: Iter 11 — verified Tenant Debts Dashboard (A1-A4) + MAX_TENANTS cap + Platform Capacity Card (B1-B3). Backend: 12/12 pytest cases PASS (test_iter11_features.py). Frontend Playwright: all 4 capacity sub-cards render with correct content (8/500 = 1.6% tenants, 9 databases, ~70% memory, ~35% CPU+disk). Tenant-debts tab renders with all required data-testids, 2 debt rows (TEST TEST 300 dz + FOAD 100 dz, total=400), remind button shows success toast and increments count, PDF button triggers actual file download (statement_TEST_TEST.pdf, 2986 bytes, valid %PDF-1.x header). Auto-refresh of platform-stats observed within the 30s window.
action_items: OPTIONAL: PDF statement uses Helvetica which doesn't render Arabic glyphs — the tenant name appearing as ASCII (e.g. 'TEST TEST') works fine, but Arabic tenant names will render as boxes. Consider registering an Arabic-capable font (e.g. NotoSansArabic) via reportlab.pdfbase.pdfmetrics if Arabic statements become a requirement.

OPTIONAL: tenant-debts list endpoint runs 1+N queries (one per wallet to fetch tenant + last reminder + count). For 100+ tenants this becomes O(3N) round-trips. Consider a single aggregation pipeline ($lookup saas_tenants + $lookup tenant_debt_reminders with $group). Acceptable for current scale (8 tenants).

OPTIONAL: MAX_TENANTS cap is read from env on every request (registration_routes.py:18, tenants_routes.py:246, platform_stats_routes.py:22). Three independent _max_tenants helpers — could be extracted into a shared util.
critical_code_review_comments: platform_stats_routes.py — _max_tenants() defaults to 0 (unlimited) when MAX_TENANTS is unset or invalid. ValueError-only catch in the try/except may miss other parse issues, but since the int() falls back via the `or 0` short-circuit, it's safe. OK.
tenant_debts_routes.py:88 — reminders_sent is computed by a count_documents call inside the loop. With N wallets that's N round-trips. Fold into the same $lookup as last_reminder_at for performance.

tenant_debts_routes.py:91 — items are sorted in Python after the DB query; if `only_with_debt=false` and many tenants exist, the resulting list could be large. Move sort to MongoDB ({'credit_debt': -1}) for consistency.

tenant_debts_routes.py:138 — payload may be None; the `payload or {}` guard handles it. Note: when FastAPI receives no body for a POST with an Optional[dict] param, it sets payload=None — current code is correct.

email_service.py:47 — module-level send_email returns False on failure but tenant_debts_routes wraps it in try/except and ignores the boolean return. That means `delivered=True` is set even if send_email returned False. Minor: consider `delivered = await send_email(...) is True` so the response field accurately reflects delivery.

PlatformCapacityCard — visual progress bar color thresholds (emerald<75%, amber<90%, red≥90%) appear consistent with the severity calculation in platform_stats_routes (warning≥80%, critical≥95%). The UI thresholds and backend severity thresholds are NOT identical — UI uses 75/90, backend uses 80/95. Minor inconsistency; align if you want UI color and backend severity to convey the same warning level.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (capacity card 4/4 sub-cards + debts tab full flow incl. remind toast + PDF download)
